record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Ergodicity for the three-parameter Volterra family
record.original_question: Consider the three-dimensional Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^2 defined by x' = x (1 + a y - b z), y' = y (1 - a x + c z), z' = z (1 + b x - c y), where a, b, c are in [-1,1]. The paper proves that if a, b, and c are all nonzero and have the same sign, then the ergodic theorem fails for this operator. Determine whether one can formulate a sufficient condition for the ergodic theorem to hold for this family, and in particular whether the parameter-sign condition appearing in Theorem 3 is sharp for separating ergodic and non-ergodic behavior.

evidence.quote: V : S2 → S2  x′ = x (1 + ay − bz) , y ′ = y (1 − ax + cz) , z ′ = z (1 + bx − cy) , where a, b, c ∈ [−1, 1].
Theorem 3. [3] If the parameters a, b, c for the Volterra QSO (9) have the same sign and each is non-zero, then the ergodic theorem will fail for this operator.
Problem 4. Is the condition of Theorem 3 sufficient for the ergodic theorem to hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2 = \{(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x,y,z \ge 0,\ x+y+z = 1\}$ be the two-dimensional simplex. For parameters $a,b,c \in [-1,1]$, define the Volterra quadratic stochastic operator $V : S^2 \to S^2$ by
\[
x' = x(1 + ay - bz),\qquad y' = y(1 - ax + cz),\qquad z' = z(1 + bx - cy).
\]
For an initial point $p \in S^2$, denote the trajectory by $V^n(p)$, and say that the ergodic theorem holds for $V$ if for every $p \in S^2$ the Cesàro averages
\[
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} V^k(p)
\]
converge as $n \to \infty$.

It is known that if $a$, $b$, $c$ are all nonzero and have the same sign, then the ergodic theorem fails for $V$. The problem is the following:

(a) Determine whether the condition that $a,b,c$ are all nonzero and of the same sign is also necessary for failure of the ergodic theorem; equivalently, determine whether for all remaining parameter choices $(a,b,c) \in [-1,1]^3$ (i.e., when at least one of $a,b,c$ is zero or the nonzero ones do not all share the same sign) the ergodic theorem holds for $V$.

(b) More generally, give a sufficient condition on $(a,b,c) \in [-1,1]^3$ under which the ergodic theorem holds for the operator $V$.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works (e.g., "Ergodic Volterra Quadratic Transformations of the Simplex," arXiv:1205.3841, and later surveys/chapters such as "Ergodic Volterra Quadratic Mappings of the Simplex," 2024) provide a description of ergodic properties of Volterra QSOs on the 2-simplex and analyze the parameter regimes (cases where parameters have mixed signs versus all-same-sign), indicating that the same-sign nonzero condition is essentially the obstruction to ergodicity, with full analyses given in special cases. The original sharpness/sufficiency question thus appears to have been substantially addressed but is reported across several papers with case-by-case analyses rather than a single unified theorem in the original formulation.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic Volterra Quadratic Transformations of Simplex
status_evidence.snippet: A Volterra quadratic stochastic operator of a three dimensional simplex into itself ... full description of ergodic properties.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodic properties of three-dimensional Volterra QSOs have been described in follow-up work.

status_evidence.title: A prey–predator model with three interacting species
status_evidence.snippet: Three cases for the parameters a, b, c: mixed signs, all positive, all negative; in case of all same sign trajectories approach heteroclinic cycles and ergodic hypothesis does not hold.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent analysis confirms parameter-sign condition governs ergodic vs. non-ergodic behavior.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic Volterra Quadratic Mappings of the Simplex
status_evidence.snippet: Complete analysis of the asymptotic behavior of trajectories of Volterra quadratic mappings of the three-dimensional simplex.
status_evidence.claim: A complete asymptotic analysis is presented in later literature.
